questions.question: Explain how the panic button's specification is read as a logic gate, show why the alternative gate fails, and describe how the two output devices are connected and why.
questions.expected_answer: The specification says the alarm must sound when the bed, stove or toilet button is pressed alone or in any combination and must be silent when none is pressed, which as logic with inputs B, S and T and output A says A is 1 when any input is 1 and 0 only when all are 0, the definition of a three-input OR gate, built from switches in parallel, so the heart of the circuit is three push switches in parallel between the battery and the alarm, with the gate read off the specification rather than assumed. Three switches in series would be a three-input AND that sounds only when all three buttons are pressed simultaneously, impossible for one person in two rooms, so it would fail the specification in every row but the last. The specification requires a loud alarm and a bright light, so the output is a buzzer and a lamp placed in parallel with each other so that each receives the full battery voltage and either works if the other fails, whereas in series they would share the voltage and the buzzer might not sound; an LED lamp needs a 330 ohm series resistor for a 3 volt supply with its long leg to positive, and the battery of two or three cells in series is matched to the buzzer and lamp.

questions.question: Describe the circuit diagram of the panic button with its symbols, layout and junction dots, and explain the reset, standby and toilet-lead refinements and the finishing rules.
questions.expected_answer: The battery of two or three cell symbols in series, long thin line positive and short thick line negative, labelled 3 V, sits on the left; a line from positive runs across the top, and three push-to-make switch symbols labelled B, S and T hang from it as parallel branches rejoining on a line below, with a dot at each of the six junctions; the rejoined line continues to the output where the buzzer, a half-circle with two leads, and the lamp, a circle with a cross or an LED symbol with its rectangle resistor in series, form two parallel branches with dots at their junctions before the line returns to negative. A reset is shown at Grade 8 as a toggle switch labelled R in parallel with the push switches, closed to hold the alarm on after a button is released and opened to silence it, with a note that a true self-latching circuit uses a relay introduced in Grade 9; standby current is zero because every switch is open at rest, satisfying the year-of-batteries specification, and this is noted on the diagram; the toilet switch has a longer line with a note that the real run would be weatherproof cable or a wireless button. Finishing rules are straight lines, right-angle corners, standard-size symbols not touching, a label beside every component, values for battery and resistor, the title, designer's name and date, and a partner test of listing the components and tracing positive to negative through each switch alone.

questions.question: Write out the panic button's truth table with its rule in words, describe the row-by-row bench test and how a failed row locates a fault, and describe the specification tests beyond the table.
questions.expected_answer: With inputs B, S and T there are eight rows counted in binary, 000, 001, 010, 011, 100, 101, 110, 111, and output A is 0 for the first row only, where no button is pressed, and 1 for the other seven, with an observed column added for testing and the rule stated as: the alarm sounds when any one or more of the three buttons is pressed and is silent only when none is pressed. The circuit is built from the diagram one lead at a time with no button pressed and checked before the battery is connected, then each row is set and the buzzer and lamp observed: nothing pressed gives silence and dark, 0, and every other combination, toilet only, stove only, stove and toilet, bed only, bed and toilet, bed and stove, all three, gives buzzer and lamp, 1, so eight matches verify the table and the test is dated and signed. A failed row locates the fault: the toilet button alone doing nothing while others work means an open toilet branch from a loose lead or dead switch, and an alarm sounding with nothing pressed means a switch wired closed or two leads touching. Beyond the table, loudness is tested by hearing the buzzer across the room and seeing the lamp from the door, the reset by the toggle holding the alarm on after release and silencing it when opened, and standby by an ammeter in the main line reading zero with nothing pressed, each recorded as met or not met, giving the diagram, table and test record the examiner requires.
